The range of $\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡x$ is given by

$$
0\le \theta \le \pi .
$$

Note that the angle $\theta $ spans the first and second quadrants.

Since $-\frac{1}{2}$ is negative, our answer is an angle that lies in the second quadrant, where cosine is negative.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14035417/assets/dbf36192ac332dc49ed75278838e989a37ac7d888311be1b8b059a7b59667aa6.png)

From the values in the second quadrant, we see that

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
